content: Spouses married February 1997 under legal community property, separated 2011 (final). Wife sought division of real estate (marital home, warehouse, land), registered movables (motorcycles, car), shares, insurance policies, bank accounts. Husband agreed to division but contested asset composition, counterclaimed including additional assets (wife's car, furniture, compensation for garage occupation). Articles 177, 179, 191, 720, 791 Italian Civil Code and Code of Civil Procedure govern immediate/residual community, personal property exceptions, dissolution timing, indivisible property sale. Issues concerned which assets fell within community property, convenient divisibility determination, and compensation for exclusive use. Registered movables (two Yamaha motorcycles purchased during marriage) fell within Article 177 immediate community but husband claimed sale—no evidence provided of sale timing, price obtained, or consumption prior to marriage end. Division request rejected absent proof. Renault Clio (purchased January 2007, initially husband's name, transferred to wife January 2009) fell within community; given indivisibility and no assignment request, Article 720 requires auction sale. Alfa Romeo (purchased by wife 2011) not community property: dissolution occurred upon separation petition filing (June 2010), not judgment finalization—purchase post-dissolution excludes from division. Shares and insurance policies fall within immediate community as investments determining credit right establishment and asset increase—purchases per Article 177(a). Parmalat shares valued €1,140, Italia shares €2,508; husband owes wife 50% share (€1,824). Postal bonds claim rejected absent documentation—disclosure request inadmissible as exploratory without prima facie evidence. Current account balances subject to residual community only if positive balance existing at dissolution—no evidence of balances or amounts, claim rejected. Movable property (marital home furnishings) divided per court-appointed expert plan into two equal-value lots assigned respectively. Real estate (Alcamo apartment, warehouses) deemed indivisible per expert: convenient divisibility requires structural feasibility creating independently enjoyable portions without excessive costs and no significant depreciation. Physical division would deprive parts of essential structural/functional characteristics, create portions unsuitable for economic function, incapable of independent enjoyment, significantly depreciated. Article 720 auction sale ordered—neither party requested assignment with excess charge. Land in Partinico inadmissible for division: currently subject to seizure in enforcement proceedings initiated by plaintiff—division belongs to enforcement judge's functional competence per Articles 599 et seq. Compensation for garage occupation rejected: no evidence provided regarding exclusive use or occupation preventing other party's access.
